reviewer: Pickle: official-source portable winter heat pack comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. Korea Consumer Agency consumer safety alert (2018-12-05, kca.go.kr): 226 heat-pack injury reports to CISS over 3.5 years (2015-2018.6.), 197 (87.2 percent) burns; of 128 burns with known severity, 63 (49.2 percent) second-degree and 55 (43.0 percent) third-degree, 92.2 percent serious; December 35 cases (26.3 percent) of 133 dated cases, 65.4 percent in winter; of 20 powder-type packs surveyed, 10 (50 percent) had incomplete usage warnings and 5 (25 percent) lacked the low-temperature-burn warning; packs sustain 10+ hours of heat, reach up to 70 C, and hold an average of 40-70 C for long periods, so direct skin contact, sleeping use, bedding use, and combining with other heating products are warned against, with children, the elderly, and people with diabetes or circulatory disorders told to avoid use. KATS safety standard for safety-confirmation household goods, notice 2026-31 effective 2026-02-17, Annex 68 (heat packs incl. pocket warmers), read on the Ministry of Government Legislation law.go.kr notice page: max temperature 70 C or below, temperature rise to 40 C within 20 minutes, duration defined as time at or above 40 C, temperature-guarantee time at or above the midpoint between peak and 40 C for at least 50 percent of duration, measured at 20 C ambient on a 30 C plate with 2 gauze and 4 cotton flannel layers over 5 samples; powder packs split into non-stick and stick-on types with a mandatory do-not-apply-directly-to-skin warning on stick-on types; military-supply packs excluded. Because the law.go.kr annex body loads only through scripts in this environment, the annex figures were cross-checked against two independent 2026-10 summaries of the same notice (babytodak.com 2026-10-25 and epickor.com 2026-09-29) and recorded consistently. MOTIE KATS and Korea Customs winter import inspection via Seoul Shinmun 2022-12-28: 340,000 non-conforming imported items seized across 16 product groups, about 140,000 of them heat packs, with one pack measured at 82.5 C against the 70 C limit; seized goods held at customs and returned or destroyed if not fixed. Aviation battery rules from AVSEC365 (Korea Transportation Safety Authority), hand-warmer lithium battery page (cntNo=1070): spare lithium-ion batteries are carry-on only and forbidden in checked baggage, 100 Wh or less permitted in reasonable personal-use quantities, over 100 to 160 Wh needs airline approval with a two-spare limit, over 160 Wh forbidden in both; lithium metal over 2 g forbidden; terminals must be insulated against short circuits; watt-hours are mAh times volts divided by 1000, and the general dangerous-goods page (cntNo=1050) notes violations can draw fines or penalties up to 20 million KRW under the Aviation Safety Act and that each airline can tighten rules further. Jin Air notice 2025-09-26 (agent.jinair.com, seq=415): wireless heating devices with built-in batteries including hand warmers are not allowed in carry-on or checked baggage; only devices with a removable battery plus airplane mode may be carried in the cabin with airline approval, batteries removed and terminals short-circuit protected, overhead-bin storage prohibited. First aid from MOIS Safety TV (safetv.go.kr idx=1254): cool the burn under gently flowing tap water that is not too cold for 10-20 minutes; never apply ice or ice water directly (vascular constriction slows recovery and raises infection risk); never pop blisters; disinfect and cover with clean gauze. Low-temperature burn background from Gyeonggi Provincial Council webzine: low-temperature burns develop at about 40-50 C with prolonged exposure, a 70 C hot pack held against skin for 2+ hours can burn, and the Kormedi 2010 dermatologist interview adds skin can start first-degree burning at 45 C. Product figures from three Coupang product pages verified in-browser on 2026-10-31: Happyday pocket hot pack 150 g, 30 pcs at 13,560 KRW (list 15,420, 12 percent off, 452 KRW per pack, 60,247 reviews, KC B685H0008-23001, product 7746926863); Smati 5000 mAh dual-side rechargeable hand warmer power bank with pouch and cable at 7,900 KRW (list 11,900, 33 percent off, 467 reviews, model PR-HWP5000, product 9031842153, seller Q&A answers confirm KC safety and EMC certification); Haruon stick-on hot pack 50 g, 10 pcs at 4,850 KRW (list 4,900, 52,033 reviews, KC B685H0011-6002, product 8391768862, 3-pack 11,380 KRW). The Haruon pharmacy listing (hkmedi.co.kr) supplies the maker label values 63 C maximum and 15-hour duration, a 3-year shelf life, and warnings against sleeping use, direct skin contact, bedding or heater proximity, with a once-per-hour skin check. Derived cost figures are recorded in the research calculations: pocket packs at 452 KRW each cost 904 KRW per day for two and 27,120 KRW per month; stick-on at 485 KRW per patch cost 970 per day and 29,100 per month; a 7,900 KRW rechargeable hand warmer pays for itself in about 8.7 (about 9) days on the two-a-day pattern; the 3-pack of stick-on works out to about 3,793 KRW per pack or about 379 KRW per patch, about 106 KRW cheaper per patch. Plan deviations: the plan's stick-on 63 C was described as the display-standard maximum, but the Korean Annex 68 standard sets 70 C for all heat packs and 63 C is the individual product label value (Haruon), so the guide presents 63 C as a representative product label and 70 C as the legal ceiling; the plan's aviation claim that rechargeable hand warmers may be carried in the cabin up to 160 Wh holds for spare lithium-ion batteries under AVSEC365 rules, but Jin Air's 2025-09-26 notice bans built-in-battery wireless heating devices from both cabin and checked baggage unless the battery is removable with airplane mode and airline approval, so the guide and the ranking card state the airline-specific stricter rule; the plan's hook statistic of about 2,000 low-temperature burn victims per year could not be verified in any primary source and was replaced with the Consumer Agency 226-case CISS statistics.
